text:
akash: Heads-up — Product wants to run a 6hr Flash Sale experiment next Tue 06:00-12:00 PST. They expect a hard 30m spike then a sustained uplift. Need a quick capacity plan for text-gen (low-latency) and a fallback routing strategy. Any obvious red flags?

maria: Can you drop the traffic shape & tokens per request? Need numbers to convert to GPU-hours.

akash: Sure — rough forecast from Product: avg tokens/request = 120, p95 tokens = 220. Baseline QPS = 500. Expected: initial spike = ~8x baseline (~4k QPS) for 30m; sustained = ~3x (~1.5k QPS) for remaining 5.5h. Using opt-7b quantized variant (we expect ~200-300 RPS per A100 depending on batch).

devon: Quick calc (ballpark): to hit 4k QPS at 250 RPS/GPU -> ~16 GPUs concurrently for model inference. That seems low vs our old numbers because of batching. Are those per-GPU RPS numbers for the exact model/config?

akash: Good catch — Product assumed optimistic batching. From last benchmark with similar traffic pattern we saw ~180 RPS/GPU at 200 token avg, p95 latency ~220ms with continuous batching. Using 180 RPS -> spike needs ~22 GPUs. But remember we need headroom for network, loadgen bursts, and other tenants.

maria: I'll convert to GPU-hours: 22 GPUs * 0.5h = 11 GPU-hours for spike. Sustained: 1.5k QPS / 180 RPS ≈ 8.5 GPUs -> round to 10 GPUs. 10 GPUs * 5.5h = 55 GPU-hours. Total ~66 GPU-hours. Add 25% safety -> ~83 GPU-hours. Cost estimate @ $3.80/GPU-hr -> ~$315.

olivia: APAC note: apac-gcr1 quota is tight this week. We can only provision up to 60 GPUs there and cross-region egress is constrained. If Product wants global rollout at launch, we should push US/ EU first and failover APAC traffic to us-west until capacity freed.

devon: Ops-wise we should prewarm caches and KV for top prefixes. Also suggest preparing a quantized fallback model (opt-7b-q) with lower memory but slightly lower quality, so routing can switch automatically if latency > p99 threshold.

akash: Agreed. Can we do an autoscale policy like: min=baseline reserved, target_util=60%, burst_pool=+30 GPUs, cooldown=120s? Also enable canary route: 10% traffic to canary in us-east for the first 20m.

maria: Draft autoscale snippet for infra team:
```json
{
  "policy": "cpu/gpu_util",
  "target": 0.6,
  "min": 10,
  "max_burst": 30,
  "cooldown_s": 120
}
```

maria: We'll need a booking for burst GPUs in Dedicated (if Product expects repeated runs). If this is one-off, suggest reserved burst + short-term on-demand. Ops, can you confirm provisioning lead time?

devon: On-demand is available but warmup of model caches is the real time sink (2-5m per replica). We should spin replicas 10m before the spike and run the prewarm script. I'll paste the loadtest command to simulate: 
```bash
./scripts/loadgen.py --target-qps 4000 --tokens 120 --model opt-7b-q --duration 1800 --warmup 600
```

olivia: I've checked region capacity: eu-west has spare GPUs; we can use eu-west as a fallback for APAC traffic if egress cost acceptable. Estimated egress cost for cartabackup routing ~ $0.02/GB — likely fine for short window. Also need to ensure our peering isn't throttled; filed a ticket to netops (NET-1832).

akash: Good. Product asks about cost vs ROI. Maria's estimate (~$315) looks low vs Product's expectation — they planned for $1.2k. We should present both conservative & optimistic numbers + a brief runbook of fallbacks.

sre-bot: [automated check] Infra snapshot: us-east GPU pool healthy, 82% allocatable; eu-west 65%; apac-gcr1 92% (quota close). Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/flash-sale-forecast (green/yellow).

devon: Decision proposal: 1) Canary in us-east 10% for 20m. 2) Prewarm + spin replicas 10m before spike. 3) Reserve burst + 25% headroom. 4) Fallback: opt-7b-q in eu-west, route APAC -> us-west if apac quota hit. 5) Ops to run a dry-run on Thu with 50% load.

akash: +1 to all. Ops/Finance: please confirm burst booking and PO by EOD Fri. I'll schedule the dry-run and post the exact ramp schedule.

maria: I'll update runbook and put the autoscale policy in infra repo. Will post PR for review. :thumbsup:
